__NEWSECTIONLINK__ ==Request for Feedback: Bureaucrats== {{discussion top|Closing as {{done|successful}}. The vast majority of users support the changes of policy with relation to [[TestWiki:Bureaucrats]]. With a successful RfC here, consuls will undertake a review of all active bureaucrats to determine which users will retain rights. [[User:BrandonWM|BrandonWM]] ([[User talk:BrandonWM|talk]] - [[Special:Contributions/BrandonWM|contribs]]) 20:36, 17 March 2025 (UTC)}} While Bureaucrat has historically been implemented as a testing role, the low requirements for entry into the role coupled with broad/disruptive permission sets has made it a prime target for bad actors - repeat instances of malicious abuse of Bureaucrat permissions necessitating intervention by global volunteers has made clear that a change is needed. Simultaneously, the relatively small number of active testwiki Consuls has meant that policy enforcement activities haven't always gotten timely action and oversight, and assistance by trusted users is needed to keep testwiki operating as a true testing space. As such, this proposal aims to convert the Bureaucrat role from one of generic testing to one of moderate trust, eliminating the easy abuse vector while remaining readily achievable and providing consuls more support in day-to-day operations. The proposed changes to [[TW:Bureaucrats|TestWiki:Bureaucrats]] can be found [[User:Zppix/Draft/Bureaucrats#Proposed Page Text Changes|on this draft page]] under the Proposed Page Text Changes section. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 10:26, 11 March 2025 (UTC) ===Support=== #{{Support|strong}} as proposer Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 10:29, 11 March 2025 (UTC) #{{Support|strong}} it was about time! Unfortunately the few are creating issues for the masses.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   10:32, 11 March 2025 (UTC) #{{support}} it's unfortunate that it has to come down to this, but there have been too many recent cases of abuse and I believe it's too easy for people to "farm" their way into getting the bureaucrat right for malicious purposes. I believe these requirements look good. [[User:Ternera|Ternera]] ([[User talk:Ternera|talk]]) 13:55, 11 March 2025 (UTC) #{{support}} Per above. [[User:Fusionium|Fusionium]] ([[User talk:Fusionium|talk]]) 19:58, 11 March 2025 (UTC) #{{Support}} Per the above. [[User:MacFan4000|MacFan4000]] ([[User talk:MacFan4000|Talk]] [[Special:Contributions/MacFan4000|Contribs]]) 03:34, 13 March 2025 (UTC) # Because a similar situation happened over there at Test Wiki (a non-Miraheze project) from a rights abuser, I {{support}} this. [[User:Codename Noreste|'''''Codename Noreste''''']] ([[User talk:Codename Noreste|talk]]) 05:00, 13 March 2025 (UTC) ===Oppose=== # {{Oppose|Strong}} Per my comments below [[User:Harvici|Harvici]] ([[User talk:Harvici|''talk'']]) 11:07, 13 March 2025 (UTC) ===Comments=== # {{Comment}} while I do support this proposal overall, I am unsure if it is necessary to grant crats abuse filter rights, instead of keeping [[TestWiki:Abuse filter operators]] as a separate role. Also not entirely sure as to the need for global lock-whitelist. —[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] ([[User talk:PixDeVl|talk]]) 16:20, 11 March 2025 (UTC) #:@[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] The idea behind this change is an in between Consuls and the non-testing rights, for a lack of a better analogy think GA vs Stewards. Regarding the globalblock-whitelist, that right is already currently given to crats as is. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 16:40, 11 March 2025 (UTC) # {{Comment}} I would prefer to stop or suspend granting bureaucrat rights to new requestors or restrict the promotion until another criteria is met.
---[[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 04:18, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #:@[[User:Imamy|Imamy]] There is currently no precedence or policy for suspending granting rights in this type of situation, and I do not believe that this warrants changing that. This discussion will likely only remain open for 7 days, and which it will be closed. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 08:55, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #::I preferred to stop or suspend new additions so that the role could remain a Test Role. A reason such as maintenance would be sufficient, such as the paring down the list comprised of inactives. However, a conversion of the role to moderator will make this role off limits to the bulk of the community. #::I would prefer creating a custom companion role to the Consul to emphasize and reinforce that a Bureaucrat is role that comes standard with a Wiki, that it is a role that allows one to manage a wiki. #::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 02:34, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #:::Making the role a non test role is precisely the intention, since as I see it, there is basically zero legitimate value to having crat for testing over sysop alone except for RfP clerking(a non test duty) and potential abuse. '''''[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] [[User Talk:PixDeVl|talk to me!]]''''' 03:11, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #::::We should just remove more rights from the Bureaucrat. I may be wrong but I don't feel that the wikis from request a wikis are that powerful as the crats here. #::::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 03:30, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #:::::The crat group is already, as I said, useless as a testing role, as is clearly evident from it’s [[Special:ListGroupRights#bureaucrat|permissions]], removing more rights does effectively nothing except maybe making it even more useless in its one non test role, and contributes nothing to solving any issues. '''''[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] [[User Talk:PixDeVl|talk to me!]]''''' 04:01, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #::::::In my opinion, all standard roles are useless as test roles. They don't compare to an actual wiki because permanence is lacking. #::::::I noticed that these roles have helped the users grow as communicators. They are more willing to voice their thoughts here than they would on Meta. Perhaps this is because this is where they get their first promotion. #::::::So if we shift the Bureaucrat to Non-Testing, I feel that it will muddy how they view Sysop role. The two roles are no longer balanced. It would be better to change both Admin and Bureaucrat to Non-Testing and then create a custom role specifically designed as a Test role. #::::::We could call the these Test roles Test-BC and Test-Admin and the users would have to submit a request for any special rights. #::::::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 01:32, 14 March 2025 (UTC) # {{Comment}} Per the draft, the current bureaucrat rights will be revoked with some exceptions. It does not state where to apply for the redefined non testing role.
--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 04:18, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #:@[[User:Imamy|Imamy]] the draft does state “Pass a Request for Permission on Community portal by community consensus” Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 08:50, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #::I guess it does say that. Thank you. --- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 02:10, 13 March 2025 (UTC) # {{Comment}} The edit count requirement has been gradually lowered even on Meta. I think that the type of qualifications necessary for a trusted position should be clarified. As long as we borrow criteria based on other wikis (even if that wiki is Meta), it will be the same volunteers from the same pool that qualify.
--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 04:48, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #:@[[User:Imamy|Imamy]] I appreciate this concern, and it was something I considered when writing this up, however, I think keeping the requirements as noted in the draft initially is best to start out. With this change a lot of caveats and precedence will need to be made, or figured out. I think at a later date, we could revisit the requirements, and see if they need to be changed or not. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 08:53, 12 March 2025 (UTC) # {{Comment}} A clause should be added allowing users in good standing on other wikis, such as Wikimedia projects, to obtain bureaucrat rights without meeting the criteria listed here. Additionally, users who currently hold bureaucrat rights should be exempt from these criteria. Since they have not demonstrated any misuse of these rights since obtaining them, they should be considered trusted.[[User:Harvici|Harvici]] ([[User talk:Harvici|''talk'']]) 18:10, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #:@[[User:Harvici|Harvici]] Simply put, no. Everyone will have to go through the same process to obtain the right. Furthermore, per the changes that are drafted, when this is enacted all bureaucrats will be removed, unless a Consul, at their discretion determines a specific user is allowed to retain them, a large number of bad actors have unfortunately ruined it for everyone. The whole point of this change is to make it a non-testing permission allowing all 47 people to retain the rights negates the entire reason for this change. Realistically there is absolutely zero reason someone can not just use sysop to test, bureaucrat does not add any practical testing value. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 18:30, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #::I agree. Most of us are fully focussed on Miraheze. Only a few volunteers still are active on Wikimedia projects. If we would make exception for Wikimedia, I feel that we then also should be as welcoming to volunteers from other wikifarms/hosts, like wiki.gg or Fandom. That is just impossible to keep track of. #::So I agree with @[[User:Zppix|Zppix]] here. It's best that everyone goes through the same process of being active on Miraheze. Also necessary, as we are not Wikimedia, but Miraheze.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   19:05, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #::This proposal rightly aims to prevent "bad actors" from misusing crat to harm the project, and the outlined criteria are effective in that regard. However, it heavily restricts the core purpose of this project—allowing users to test tools like crat and sysop in a controlled environment. Users unfamiliar with these tools, whether from Wikimedia, Fandom, or wiki.gg, may want to explore them out of curiosity, and trusted users from these platforms should be exempt from strict limitations. #::You mentioned that {{tq|[the] whole point of this change is to make it a non-testing permission}}, but shouldn’t the focus be on restricting bad actors while ensuring trusted users can still test it? If the goal is solely to block bad actors, the policy should allow trusted crats to grant the right to users they personally trust, even if those users don’t meet the edit or account age requirements. Any misuse could then result in revocation and disciplinary measures against both parties. Otherwise, the policy risks being overly restrictive rather than protective. #::And regarding {{tq|bureaucrat does not add any practical testing value}}, what about Nuke and MassMessage? [[User:Harvici|Harvici]] ([[User talk:Harvici|''talk'']]) 11:06, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #:::"Trust is earned slowly, but lost in a blink of an eye". #:::You state ''trusted users from these platforms should be exempt from strict limitations''. #:::Who decides whether they are trusted, and who are not? Does it imply that we for each user have to research whether they are in a good standing on their respective platforms? And what means trusted for one, might not be for another. #:::I am a trusted user here on Miraheze, as I have proven myself. But I am banned on Danish Wikipedia in a period where it didn't go well with me. And remember that Wikimedia standards are way different then ours here. The same goes for Wiki.gg and Fandom as well as other platforms. Each have their own standards. #:::That is why I believe that the only real trust one could measure against the requirements, is the trust that has been earned on Miraheze.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   16:45, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #::::A new EnWiki admin looking to test the Nuke and MassMessage tools without disrupting en wiki finds this project through a quick google search but discovers they must be an established Miraheze user to proceed.Shouldn't he be "trusted enough" and believed to be responsible enough to not use such tools in a abuse manner.However at the same time, a known LTA on EnWiki should not be trusted. [[User:Harvici|Harvici]] ([[User talk:Harvici|''talk'']]) 17:16, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #:::::If someone from Wikimedia, as per your example situation would want to test those things, they are luck, Wikimedia provides a testwiki where they can request such permissions, see test.wikipedia.org. Special:Nuke is too prone to abuse to continue to allow it to be a test permission. Furthermore, it is very very rare for anyone on Public Test Wiki to have ever used mass message anyway. #:::::Using someone’s presence and history on another platform is unreliable, just because they behave on Wikimedia, or Fandom, doesn’t mean they won’t come here to cause issues, nor can we reliably confirm that a user is who they say they are on another platform. #:::::Public Test Wiki is meant to be a place where people can test things for valid reasons, not a place where we blindly give people rights. This is still very much a real breathing project with rules, and guidelines that need to be followed. It is not a place for chaos, abuse and lawlessness. #:::::I have yet to see any compelling arguments for why those 2 specific rights have any value for testing. Sysop grants practically anything someone would need to reasonably test. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 17:47, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #::::::I would like to point out that the test and test2 Wikipedias are for devs to test code before it goes live and those projects specifically say they are not a place for people to test tools. Instead, they point users to these projects (https://test.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Requests/Tools). I still am in favor of restricting the bureaucrat right, but wanted to show where Wikimedians are coming from. [[User:Ternera|Ternera]] ([[User talk:Ternera|talk]]) 18:22, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #:::::::Yeah, considering how unknown I feel the WMF test wikis are I would not count their existence too strongly here. '''''[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] [[User Talk:PixDeVl|talk to me!]]''''' 18:30, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #:::My thoughts on this is that the issue of turning BC into a non test group and the Nuke/MMS rights don’t need to be bundled together. We can make crat a non test role and still provide an avenue for some users (Wikimedians and others) to use those test powers. I don’t think Nuke and MMS can be rolled into freebie sysop, but I believe it would be feasible to split them into one or two more advanced testing roles that are fine to give out but still be a bit more restricted, where consuls and crats to grant to users where’s there’s a reasonable assurance they won’t cause a problem with the bigger tools, like how [[TW:Abuse filter operators|Abuse filter operators]] function. That’s a case in which I think it would be fine to take experience and such from Wikimedia and other projects into account. '''''[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] [[User Talk:PixDeVl|talk to me!]]''''' 18:42, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #::::In my time on Public Test Wiki, I think I have maybe seen Mass Message used for testing a grand total of 4 times. The value of having that as a testing right is negibile. Honestly, I think at a later time after this new change is implemented we could revisit this, but I think as of right now, it really is out of scope for this proposed change. #::::Nuke frankly is a hard no from me. Too much damage in one click can be done, and has previously been used to mass abuse. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 19:09, 13 March 2025 (UTC) #::::Alternatively: If a Wikimedian can prove that they are who they are, and there is a legitimate reason for testing it, it could be discussed on a case by case perhaps. But that would need to be discussed in the wider range of volunteers (Consuls, Stewards). #::::But really, why would someone need to test such function? Wouldn't reading the documentation on the extension page sufficing? #::::And I agree with Zppix that this is a subject for another RfF/RfC at another time.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   20:28, 13 March 2025 (UTC) # {{comment}} from a few different angles including to address thoughts of other comments and votes. #* A reset of granted rights is indeed necessary because the scope and responsibility of BC is changed with this proposal. This has precedence when CVT was changed to global sysop on Meta in the past and is reasonable when changes are this drastic. I haven't looked at the list of bureaucrats in order to provide an example, but I don't believe confirmations should be a shoo-in either: absence of abusive conduct is not a case for more advanced responsibility. The fairest outcome imo is a full revote rather than selective retention. #* Disabling global blocks locally should not be in the permissions list because it has no real testing or even administrative value here I believe. In the best case, it marginally increases registration convenience in niche cases but the better answer to that would be creating an account for the affected user and/or making CVT/stewards aware of an inappropriate block. Being available here even at higher trust greatly increases a scenario of the worst case, in which global sanction can be evaded. I have this same concern about it being available globally to wikis in general so this is not a unique concern to me. #* Abuse filter is dangerous, but alright. #* A great deal of leeway is granted to consuls to change sweeping portions of the role and access as they see fit. I'm not entirely against this but the ability to modify responsibilities at will seems heavy. # In general this represents a step forward that I approve of. --'''[[User:Raidarr|raidarr]]''' '''('''[[User_talk:Raidarr|💬]]''')''' 22:20, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #:Just to reiterate my response off-wiki: #::*Regarding your first point, selective retention is best, it will be decided by active consuls on who will retain the right based on the proposed eligibility requirements, trust, and history of the user. Starting with 0 bureaucrats would be detrimental to Public TestWiki as then all responsibilities would fall to Consuls until such new bureaucrats could be elected. On the flip side, there is no reason to have ~47 bureaucrats after the change either. #::*Regarding your second point, the only change I proposed regarding the rights of the group was making it so they could no longer grant bureaucrat, the rest of the rights remained the same. The globalblock-whitelist right being granted to the group, in my opinion, has a no major impact either way. This can be revisited later on if it becomes an issue. #::*Regarding your third point, AbuseFilter usage will likely be minimal, Public Test Wiki more so relies on the global filters rather than any substantial local ones. #::*Regarding your final point, considering the idea behind this change is to have bureaucrats effectively become the in between of Consuls and testing rights, and the fact they will be working very closely with Consuls, it makes sense to have a clause that allows Consuls discretion, however, I do not foresee this being something that is used very often, and even less so as the scope and overall new changes get fleshed out as time goes on. This very much is more of don’t drown the Consuls in paperwork while we figure out how things will work, and during an urgent situation type provision. #:Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 18:01, 13 March 2025 (UTC) # {{Comment}}     I would be in favor of changing both standard roles to Non-Testing and then create a Test role made solely for testing. However I am not in favor if one is a Non-Testing role and the other is a Test role. That will only create confusion and require a history lesson.
Also, there really is no reason to explain to anyone further than a Test Wiki is a Developer's Sandbox. The name Test Wiki [[TestWiki:Community_portal#c-Ternera-20250313182200-Zppix-20250313174700|now makes sense to me.]]
I resisted using Test Wiki for as long as I had because I couldn't really see how this site could be used for testing by the average user due to the requirement that user must '''revert''' all changes after the test was done.
However, by holding the Admin position, it did help to clarify somewhat what it feel like to be an Admin on a Wiki. Other than that, the Test Wiki provides a place for experimentation which seems to be the root of the issues that this proposal is trying to curb. Hence I'm open to changing Bureaucrat to Non-Testing if the same could be done for Admin. I was hoping to keep Bureaucrat a Testing role because it would be easier to talk about two like roles than to instruct users about why they are so different.
--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 02:57, 14 March 2025 (UTC) #:This does not make sense to me. Testwiki's sole function is testing what are admin-grade tools. Blocking, page operations, and so forth; if this was confusing it is an error of presentation. The only bureaucrat capabilities to test are leadership skills and ManageWiki. Neither are feasible here. It is intuitive to consider admin/sysop as testing what can reasonably be granted openly on mediawiki like this, bureaucrat as a more senior tester who helps keep things running, and finally consul to be the last line/make calls. I'm not against renaming BC altogether if it helps but I'm not sure what name would be suitable. --'''[[User:Raidarr|raidarr]]''' '''('''[[User_talk:Raidarr|💬]]''')''' 09:02, 15 March 2025 (UTC) #::Offering Clarification in case we are not looking at the same point. #::I'm opposed to changing the role description from Testing to Non-Testing because it makes no sense to make Bureaucrat Non-Testing and then keep Admin as a Testing role. #::I feel this proposal isn't just about raising the requirements, it's about changing definition of the roles themselves. I don't feel that there is any reason to change the definitions. The current document already states the position has to be earned. We could keep the documents as they are and then focus on limiting who can promote someone to Bureaucrat. Perhaps just demote everyone back to Admin to start a fresh cycle. I feel there are so many things we can do without changing the documents themselves. #::* [[User:Zppix/Draft/Bureaucrats#Proposed_Page_Text_Changes|draft]] #::* [[TestWiki:Bureaucrats]] #::* [[TestWiki:Administrators]] #::[[User:Zppix/Draft/Bureaucrats#Proposed_Page_Text_Changes| Draft states that Bureaucrat will stop being a Test role]]: #:::Bureaucrat is a non-testing permission that allows users to add administrator, and flooder permissions to other accounts. The bureaucrat permission is not easy to obtain as it is not a testing permission, and works closely with Consuls to assist with administration of TestWiki. #::[[TestWiki:Bureaucrats]] states: #::: Bureaucrat is a primarily testing permission that allows users to add administrator, bureaucrat, and flooder permissions to other accounts. The bureaucrat permission is not as easy to obtain as administrator because it can grant administrator and bureaucrat permissions. #::[[TestWiki:Administrators]] #:::Administrators are the primary user group for testing the administrator toolkit. It is granted, upon request (usually at Request permissions), to any registered user. #::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 22:01, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #::: {{tq|I feel this proposal isn't just about raising the requirements, it's about changing definition of the roles themselves}} is exactly the point of this proposal. The points being made is that crat offers no use as a test right if you already have admin, and a non test role to support Consuls is something we should have, so solve one problem with another. Resetting the members has no point to it, because there is no point to the role itself. '''''[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] [[User Talk:PixDeVl|talk to me!]]''''' 22:10, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #::::There is also no reason to complicate the definitions. If we remove the Test permission from Bureaucrat, then the Admin role should also remove the Test role so they are balanced. #::::Then if anyone needs to test, we should offer roles that are for Test purposes only. #::::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 23:08, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #:::::I think you are missing the point. #:::::# The reason for this proposal is to have Bureaucrats that can help the Consuls in the daily tasks. This is not a test role. #:::::# Admin role remains a test role so users can get acquainted with the regular admin tools. {{Aan}} == Request for Consul == I have made constructive non-test edits and I am a bureaucrat so should I become a consul? [[User:MiraEdit|MiraEdit]] ([[User talk:MiraEdit|talk]]) 23:04, 2 February 2025 (UTC) :: Please review the terms on the Test Wiki Main page [[TestWiki]], specifically the rules listed in the section [[TestWiki#Things to keep in mind]]. If you are not sure which rule was violated, you should reach out to [[m:Steward requests]] or discuss at the [[m:Community portal]]. : --- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 01:44, 3 February 2025 (UTC) ::: I know my answer didn't really answer your question, but basically, every wiki is different. Please learn more about Test Wiki if you really want to become a Consul. ::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 01:47, 3 February 2025 (UTC) == Refreshing created a test page == I was told my test page was labeled abusive because it was short and had "bad words." I opted to use the preview bar instead. Later I refreshed the page (F5) and for some reason that created it. No bad words, but the page will probably be gone by the time you see this. Posting because it said to log an issue [[User:CivicLessons|CivicLessons]] ([[User talk:CivicLessons|talk]]) 01:57, 15 February 2025 (UTC) == Can't undo == All of a sudden, I can't undo. I even went to contributions and reverted from there, but the pages still exist and have the content [[User:CivicLessons|CivicLessons]] ([[User talk:CivicLessons|talk]]) 04:30, 18 February 2025 (UTC) :Don't know which pages you are referring to. I could be wrong, but generally, we can rollback 1 and if someone has already contributed after your contribution, then rollback is not possible. :--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 02:24, 25 February 2025 (UTC) == Blocking Policy == Hey all, I am working on rewriting the blocking policy, you can see the proposed changes at [[User:Zppix/Draft/Blocking policy]]. This is '''not''' a vote, but rather a thread where people can share thoughts. The plan is to implement this either later this evening or by Tuesday, March 4th. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 18:36, 3 March 2025 (UTC) :'''Update: the updated [[Special:MyLanguage/TestWiki:Blocking policy|blocking policy]]''' is now in effect as of Monday, March 2nd 6:16PM UTC-6. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 10:45, 4 March 2025 (UTC) ::@[[User:Zppix|Zppix]] Could you summarize the changes made? Thanks! [[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] ([[User talk:Bunnypranav|talk]]) 12:01, 4 March 2025 (UTC) :::@[[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] Consuls, CVT, and Stewards are the only ones authorized to issue non-test blocks, test blocks can now only be done on accounts the user controls or on approved test accounts, appeals are only done via the blocked user’s talk page, or by emailing the blocking Consul, third party appeals are no longer accepted. I recommend reading the full policy to ensure you know the entire policy. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 12:05, 4 March 2025 (UTC) ::::Thanks for that! I obviously do not object the policy, just wanted your say on what you changed. :) [[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] ([[User talk:Bunnypranav|talk]]) 12:08, 4 March 2025 (UTC) :::::ZPPIX WHY DO YOU KEEP MAKING POLICY CHANGES WITHOUT CONSENSUS! THIS IS TYRANNY! THIS IS UNFAIR BECAUSE PEOPLE MAY HAVE VOTED A DIFFERENT OPTION! [[User:Lobby123|Lobby123]] ([[User talk:Lobby123|talk]]) 20:07, 8 May 2025 (UTC) ::::::I agree on you lobby123 [[Special:Contributions/194.195.254.140|194.195.254.140]] 20:28, 8 May 2025 (UTC) :Just for clarification to the broader TestWiki community, Consuls are the users whom have the full decision making capabilities for Public Test Wiki, and as such updating policies or otherwise are within the scope of the role. Preventing abuse is a must have on Test Wiki, so by doing so it was a Consul decision to unilaterally bring policies up to date with fresh changes to prevent bad actors. It is not Tyranny, it is how a wiki works. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 21:05, 8 May 2025 (UTC) ::I do this as well on a local wiki that isn't the test one as an admin that can enforce and change rules around to keep it up to date like yes communities are needed but not for everything that are granted rights to staff. [[User:339Breakingoof|TheFunny339YoshiPlushGuy]] ([[User talk:339Breakingoof|talk]]) 13:38, 9 May 2025 (UTC) == Request for Consul (PixDeVl) == {{Discussion top|{{done}}, welcome to the Consul team. Please reach out if you have any questions. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 11:26, 9 March 2025 (UTC)}} Hi folks, I’m filing this Request for Consul, frankly because I noticed that we currently have only 2 remotely active Consuls, being Zppix and Reception, and, even with something like PTW, having an official project wiki be run by two folks isn’t great, so I’d thought I’d offer to lend a hand. I am not very active priorly with what exists of the community on PTW, but as a current global functionary, I still think it wouldn’t hurt to have an extra hand helping keep things clean. Feel free to ask any questions regarding this, as always :) —[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] ([[User talk:PixDeVl|talk]]) 03:35, 4 March 2025 (UTC) :{{support}}  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   03:39, 4 March 2025 (UTC) :{{support}} trusted user. [[User:Ternera|Ternera]] ([[User talk:Ternera|talk]]) 04:01, 4 March 2025 (UTC) :You are not active here at all, and you have only 5 edits. Your administrator and bureaucrat permissions were enabled without a proper request and in a way that is against the rules (you cannot enable bureaucrat privileges immediately along with admin privileges, because that violates [[TW:Bureaucrats]]). I see '''[[:w:WP:HATSHOP]]''' here. Just because you have GA permissions does not automatically give you the ability to bypass local rules and jump over community norms. I cannot formally participate in the vote as an IP, but I am personally very much against this request, for the good of PTW and respect for its users. [[Special:Contributions/94.254.227.16|94.254.227.16]] 12:41, 4 March 2025 (UTC) ::When you know that @[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] is very active on Discord, Meta, Phorge, etc. you would understand that wanting to help out colleagues that need extra help, is a good thing. 5 edits here would not be a limiting factor, as you need to look at @[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]]'s activity throughout the whole of Miraheze. Not sure why you are against him, but I hope you will look at [[Special:CentralAuth/PixDeVl]] and rethink your comment, which I find a bit aggressive. And yes, the same goes for me. I am not very active here. But I am a Mirahezian at heart!  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   13:01, 4 March 2025 (UTC) :::Are we considering granting global or local permissions here? As far as I know, consul permissions are local permissions on PTW - so the candidate's '''local contributions''' should be considered first, not other global contributions. Also, PixDeVl claims to want to help, but has '''not actually done anything for PTW''' - do you grant very advanced permissions based on willingness and promises, and not on actual contribution? This is rather unusual. If PixDeVl really wanted to help, he could do so with the permissions he currently has. Please note that his activity, e.g. on RfP is none, and that is pretty much the basic form of helping PTW. PixDeVl does not need consul permissions to help on PTW. I do not rule it out in the future, but I would like to see more involvement, experience, and activity on PTW. [[Special:Contributions/94.254.227.16|94.254.227.16]] 13:47, 4 March 2025 (UTC) ::::I get that you look from the ground floor up. I have a more centered view from the MetaWiki and Discord. He is a trusted user who has been a great asset to the broader community. ::::I feel that you are gate keeping the local community, and that is your prerogative, but I think that PTW will benefit from his policy knowhow as well as his activity on the technical side. (Phorge) ::::On the other hand I find that waiting for first comments to arrive before answering on your own RfP doesn't make you to eager, as if one is collecting hats. I can assure you he's not. ::::I cannot take your concerns away, but hope you want to see it from the outside in, instead of the inside out.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   13:49, 4 March 2025 (UTC) :::::I do not believe in Quantity, but Quality. I can make 1000's of edits, but they do not tell much.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   13:50, 4 March 2025 (UTC) ::::::These are beautiful and classic words... As a result, I feel that I have gained a bit more understanding of Test Wiki. :::::::* '''Why won't he use his current permissions to help PTW?''' :::::::As I understand it, Bureaucrat and Administrator are testing roles. Edits is not the end all be all. Further, it is clear to me that there is either a lack of understanding from you on the differences between having Global user rights and local user rights. For PixDeVI their use of global rights is governed by global Miraheze policy which dictates when and when they cannot use their global rights to intervene, but them asking for local rights it is allowing them to effectively not only help us Consuls, but also allow them to act based on our local policies outside of the governance of global policy requirements which can be restrictive and ultimately lead to relying on myself or another of the very few active Consuls which can lead to delays or even missed violations. ::::Please note my above comment does not reflect a vote but rather an observation of the discussion you have started. I neither endorse or oppose the candidate. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 14:04, 4 March 2025 (UTC) ::The concern is not unfair; a user of this few edits both globally and locally seeking such a project leadership role is irregular, even with the precedent of [[Special:CentralAuth/subwayfares|subwayfares]] for wiki creation on Meta. Typically in a wiki that is fully independent this would be stranger as you would hope a leader is representative of the project, although there is merit to onboarding a trusted user in an advisory or supporting capacity. I would argue the key here is that this is ultimately a [[m:miraheze projects|Miraheze Project]]. I believe its identity as such should be a modifier for cases like this and that it is ideal for global functionaries to be more tightly bound with such a project, recommended in queue by wiki creators as it is with a domain currently hosted at WikiTide Foundation's grace. This may not be the ideal way to do it; my theory is to propose stewards as 'at large' consuls should locally invested members need a 'third opinion', more local consuls are involved and so on. Global administrators could perhaps fill the intermediary second line role bureaucrat serves, able to step in if there is backlog or an incident (short of something a GA/steward should step in for anyway). Otherwise there is a strong culture of 'separation of roles' at issue here and which is why pixel can't necessarily just jump in and do these things: it is not GS mandate. Therefore this request is an extension of his capabilities to reduce 'paperwork'. ::Essentially what I'm getting at is this request is reasonable, but skepticism of his investment in ''this'' local project holding such a role is also reasonable. And ideally, better tying the wiki to global operations through a community discussion is the best path in my opinion. The same for other projects such as dev and commons which already sort of act this way - zppix and alpad are local figures, reception and some others are global figures tied in, but as you see with the [[Special:ListUsers/consul|consul list]] it's a bit messy, outdated. ::Finally and drawing back a bit, there is no issue with an IP expressing these opinions. I would support their right to do so. I would also support a blocked user expressing a reasonable opinion to the degree I would offer to relay reasonable thoughts as food for thought even if they are blocked. An occasion where the IP editor and the blocked user overlap however is a very dangerous game that should discontinue immediately. --'''[[User:Raidarr|raidarr]]''' '''('''[[User_talk:Raidarr|💬]]''')''' 23:22, 4 March 2025 (UTC) :::I agree with Raidarr. Test Wiki is structured very differently from other types of Wikis which makes it more difficult to identify or measure a candidate's qualifications by traditional means. :::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 02:07, 5 March 2025 (UTC) :[[File:OOjs_UI_icon_help-ltr-progressive.svg|18px|link=]] '''Question''' for {{ping|PixDeVl}}
What is meant by '''an extra hand helping keep things clean'''? What kind of things?
--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 03:45, 5 March 2025 (UTC) ::@[[User:Imamy|Imamy]] TestWiki by its nature isn’t in dire need of conventional clean up work, but we have seen a recent uptick in issues where trolls go on mass desysoping sprees or otherwise cause a ruckus(something I believe Zppix has also wanted to address in policy), but as Raidarr said, PTW is an official Miraheze project, and as such, I don’t believe relying on really 2 activish functionaries to keep an eye on the place and make sure it’s tidy is viable or appropriate, hence my offering to take up the bit to properly police when issues come up beyond what’s included in the GA mandate and codified in local policy. Contrary to our anon friend, I do not claim to “need” these rights, I am offering to lend a hand to the small consul team in supplement to my other duties, and believe it would be beneficial to undergo this RFP to be able to do so without having to worry about global role scope ambiguity among other things. [[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] ([[User talk:PixDeVl|talk]]) 15:00, 5 March 2025 (UTC) :::Thank you for answering my first question. :::[[File:OOjs_UI_icon_help-ltr-progressive.svg|18px|link=]] '''Question''' followup for {{ping|PixDeVl}} :::Hypothetically, if some disruptive activities were committed with the very best of intentions due to questionable judgement, how would you help wayward testers tweak their behavior before further violations take them straight to a permanent ban? :::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 03:47, 6 March 2025 (UTC) ::::@[[User:Imamy|Imamy]] Should a user unknowingly or mistakenly violate the [[TW:Testing policy|Testing policy]], we should, as with any wiki, [[wp:assume good faith|assume good faith]] that they do not mean to purposely harm the project. That means contacting them in a civil tone to explain what they were doing and why it’s an issue, how to do whatever they want to do properly, and cleaning up. If they are acting in obvious bad faith or continue to be disruptive after multiple escalating warnings, only then should sanctions such as a serious block be applied ideally. [[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] ([[User talk:PixDeVl|talk]]) 12:53, 6 March 2025 (UTC) :{{support}} Pix is one of the most promising young volunteers we've had in the nearly 6 years I've been aorund. I am glad to have the extra support for testwiki. It is not Tyranny, it is how a wiki works. I'm not entirely against this but the ability to modify responsibilities at will seems heavy. # In general this represents a step forward that I approve of. --'''[[User:Raidarr|raidarr]]''' '''('''[[User_talk:Raidarr|💬]]''')''' 22:20, 12 March 2025 (UTC) #:Just to reiterate my response off-wiki: #::*Regarding your first point, selective retention is best, it will be decided by active consuls on who will retain the right based on the proposed eligibility requirements, trust, and history of the user. Starting with 0 bureaucrats would be detrimental to Public TestWiki as then all responsibilities would fall to Consuls until such new bureaucrats could be elected. On the flip side, there is no reason to have ~47 bureaucrats after the change either. #::*Regarding your second point, the only change I proposed regarding the rights of the group was making it so they could no longer grant bureaucrat, the rest of the rights remained the same. The globalblock-whitelist right being granted to the group, in my opinion, has a no major impact either way. This can be revisited later on if it becomes an issue. #::*Regarding your third point, AbuseFilter usage will likely be minimal, Public Test Wiki more so relies on the global filters rather than any substantial local ones. #::*Regarding your final point, considering the idea behind this change is to have bureaucrats effectively become the in between of Consuls and testing rights, and the fact they will be working very closely with Consuls, it makes sense to have a clause that allows Consuls discretion, however, I do not foresee this being something that is used very often, and even less so as the scope and overall new changes get fleshed out as time goes on. This very much is more of don’t drown the Consuls in paperwork while we figure out how things will work, and during an urgent situation type provision. #:Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 18:01, 13 March 2025 (UTC) # {{Comment}}     I would be in favor of changing both standard roles to Non-Testing and then create a Test role made solely for testing. However I am not in favor if one is a Non-Testing role and the other is a Test role. That will only create confusion and require a history lesson.
Also, there really is no reason to explain to anyone further than a Test Wiki is a Developer's Sandbox. The name Test Wiki [[TestWiki:Community_portal#c-Ternera-20250313182200-Zppix-20250313174700|now makes sense to me.]]
I resisted using Test Wiki for as long as I had because I couldn't really see how this site could be used for testing by the average user due to the requirement that user must '''revert''' all changes after the test was done.
However, by holding the Admin position, it did help to clarify somewhat what it feel like to be an Admin on a Wiki. Other than that, the Test Wiki provides a place for experimentation which seems to be the root of the issues that this proposal is trying to curb. Hence I'm open to changing Bureaucrat to Non-Testing if the same could be done for Admin. I was hoping to keep Bureaucrat a Testing role because it would be easier to talk about two like roles than to instruct users about why they are so different.
--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 02:57, 14 March 2025 (UTC) #:This does not make sense to me. Testwiki's sole function is testing what are admin-grade tools. Blocking, page operations, and so forth; if this was confusing it is an error of presentation. The only bureaucrat capabilities to test are leadership skills and ManageWiki. Neither are feasible here. It is intuitive to consider admin/sysop as testing what can reasonably be granted openly on mediawiki like this, bureaucrat as a more senior tester who helps keep things running, and finally consul to be the last line/make calls. I'm not against renaming BC altogether if it helps but I'm not sure what name would be suitable. --'''[[User:Raidarr|raidarr]]''' '''('''[[User_talk:Raidarr|💬]]''')''' 09:02, 15 March 2025 (UTC) #::Offering Clarification in case we are not looking at the same point. #::I'm opposed to changing the role description from Testing to Non-Testing because it makes no sense to make Bureaucrat Non-Testing and then keep Admin as a Testing role. #::I feel this proposal isn't just about raising the requirements, it's about changing definition of the roles themselves. I don't feel that there is any reason to change the definitions. The current document already states the position has to be earned. We could keep the documents as they are and then focus on limiting who can promote someone to Bureaucrat. Perhaps just demote everyone back to Admin to start a fresh cycle. I feel there are so many things we can do without changing the documents themselves. #::* [[User:Zppix/Draft/Bureaucrats#Proposed_Page_Text_Changes|draft]] #::* [[TestWiki:Bureaucrats]] #::* [[TestWiki:Administrators]] #::[[User:Zppix/Draft/Bureaucrats#Proposed_Page_Text_Changes| Draft states that Bureaucrat will stop being a Test role]]: #:::Bureaucrat is a non-testing permission that allows users to add administrator, and flooder permissions to other accounts. The bureaucrat permission is not easy to obtain as it is not a testing permission, and works closely with Consuls to assist with administration of TestWiki. #::[[TestWiki:Bureaucrats]] states: #::: Bureaucrat is a primarily testing permission that allows users to add administrator, bureaucrat, and flooder permissions to other accounts. The bureaucrat permission is not as easy to obtain as administrator because it can grant administrator and bureaucrat permissions. #::[[TestWiki:Administrators]] #:::Administrators are the primary user group for testing the administrator toolkit. It is granted, upon request (usually at Request permissions), to any registered user. #::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 22:01, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #::: {{tq|I feel this proposal isn't just about raising the requirements, it's about changing definition of the roles themselves}} is exactly the point of this proposal. The points being made is that crat offers no use as a test right if you already have admin, and a non test role to support Consuls is something we should have, so solve one problem with another. Resetting the members has no point to it, because there is no point to the role itself. '''''[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] [[User Talk:PixDeVl|talk to me!]]''''' 22:10, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #::::There is also no reason to complicate the definitions. If we remove the Test permission from Bureaucrat, then the Admin role should also remove the Test role so they are balanced. #::::Then if anyone needs to test, we should offer roles that are for Test purposes only. #::::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 23:08, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #:::::I think you are missing the point. #:::::# The reason for this proposal is to have Bureaucrats that can help the Consuls in the daily tasks. This is not a test role. #:::::# Admin role remains a test role so users can get acquainted with the regular admin tools. When a user has become an admin, and has been one a while, and should be entrusted the role as bureaucrat, the local bureaucrat can assist the newly appointed bureaucrat. Imho there doesn't need to be a test wiki for that, as this can be locally monitored. #:::::# This Bureaucrat role is not a role that really needs daily testing. #:::::# There are certain roles that need trust. I feel that a Bureaucrat is a role that should only be given to users with a trusted reputation. #::::: Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   23:28, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #::::::# If Bureaucrats assist Consuls, we can still remove Test role from Admin. #::::::# If we create a distinction between these 2 roles, then we make it harder to explain why Bureaucrats can't be used for Testing but may only govern and whatever they do on the regular wikis. And then in the same breath state that if you want to test, then please apply for Admin because that's a Testing role. And also if you get promoted to Bureaucrat, then you can't test on the Wiki anymore. You'll have to test off site because it's not a Testing role. #::::::# Also, if someone needs higher privileges, then a Test role similar to Bureaucrat will have to be created when it is needed. #::::::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 23:43, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #:::::::No one said a bureaucrat can’t test, it just means that it is a role that is apart of the wiki’s administration. #:::::::Administrator already has all rights that have any value in testing. So there is not reason to create any roles. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 23:47, 16 March 2025 (UTC) #::::::::No one said a bureaucrat can’t test, it just means that it is a role that is apart of the wiki’s administration. #::::::::No one has to say that a Bureaucrat Test role can't do their part to assist administration as well too. The specifics have already been outlined in the current document. #::::::::: The stranger the wording gets, the more questions that will arise. I'm sure someone will find time to play the word game. #::::::::In the end, all roles in the community require Trust. Those who get reprimanded for violations may not be aware of what constitutes as Trust. When they get their warning, they may think they broke a few rules, when they actually broke trust. #::::::::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 00:34, 17 March 2025 (UTC) #:::::::::I will put it simply. #:::::::::#Consuls are not a testing role #:::::::::#Bureaucrats are not a testing role (they were, but now it's undesired due to recent spate of abuse) #:::::::::#Admins are a testing role. They will stay like that. #:::::::::There is nothing strange in the wording, but I feel that you hate the change, and do anything to keep the status quo. #:::::::::Yes indeed. All roles require trust, but not every role can do as much harm as the Bureaucrats can. #:::::::::How users perceive their warnings has nothing to do with this discussion. #:::::::::I think it we should leave it at that as I think all points are thoroughly covered.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   10:11, 17 March 2025 (UTC) #::::::3. This Bureaucrat role is not a role that really needs daily testing #::::::I don't think anyone can test daily, not even the Admin. #::::::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 00:40, 17 March 2025 (UTC) #:::::::What I meant is... it isn't tested every day by our guests. Not that one guest is testing it daily.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   10:12, 17 March 2025 (UTC) #::::Resetting the members has no point to it, because there is no point to the role itself. #::::This works if we do not make changes to the roles. After the reset, anyone who wants to be promoted to Bureaucrat will have to provide a better reason than "testing". #::::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 23:12, 16 March 2025 (UTC) {{discussion bottom}}

body:
{{/header}} [[Category:Non-test pages]]
__NEWSECTIONLINK__ == Inactive Rights Removal - 04-03-2025 == The rights of the following users will be removed on or after 04-11-2025 if they do not return to activity: *{{RFP/User|Cactus2}} Previously expressed interest im retaining rights. *{{RFP/User|Cactusalt}} same as above. *{{RFP/User|Códigonombre Alguien}} *{{RFP/User|The God}} *{{RFP/User|ToadetteEdit}} *{{RFP/User|Toonlinky Blorb}} *{{RFP/User|Waki285}} Globally active user, exception made on their behalf. *{{RFP/User|WikiTester75}} *{{RFP/User|Wooze}} *{{RFP/User|Zippybonzo}} Holding off for now. *{{RFP/User|Zorrotesla}} *{{RFP/User|水戸特快}} *{{RFP/User|黑茶}} Thanks, :[[User:MacFan4000|MacFan4000]] ([[User talk:MacFan4000|Talk]] [[Special:Contributions/MacFan4000|Contribs]]) :For the Consul Team :22:50, 3 April 2025 (UTC) ::{{Done}} all except marked. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 12:54, 19 April 2025 (UTC) == Request for Bureaucrat == {{discussion top|Unsuccessful per clear community consensus. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 14:48, 9 April 2025 (UTC)}} Hello there as per requested in [[TestWiki:Request permissions]] and suggested I would like to request for Bureaucrat rights on this wiki as I have already worked as crat in this wiki many times and I was unable to be active for a long time due to some reasons now as per the policy for the Crat has been also changed I would like to request for crat right and I'm fully aware of the fights of crat and wouldn't use it for vandalism and use it responsibly as I had done I'm the past and now I wanna again join the team amd and contribute to the wiki. [[User:Xaloria|Xaloria]] ([[User talk:Xaloria|talk]]) 01:50, 7 April 2025 (UTC) :{{Oppose|Strong}} to this. The language here not only gives no real/specific reason for requesting the group, stating you won’t use it for vandalism as a qualification for the role indicates either a misunderstanding of the role’s purpose(what is basically now intended to function as deputy Consul), or of the standards associated with staffing this, or any official Miraheze project. '''''[[User:PixDeVl|PixDeVl]] [[User Talk:PixDeVl|talk to me!]]''''' 04:07, 7 April 2025 (UTC) :@[[User:Xaloria|Xaloria]] Could you give a brief of how you wish to use the right and contribute to the wiki? [[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] ([[User talk:Bunnypranav|talk]]) 10:47, 7 April 2025 (UTC) :{{comment}} A steward on another test wiki [https://testwiki.wiki/index.php?title=Special:Log&logid=62833 confirmed] two days ago that this user abused multiple accounts (that is, [[User:Nexora|Nexora]]). [[User:PB2008|PB2008]] ([[User talk:PB2008|talk]]) 10:18, 9 April 2025 (UTC) :{{o}} I would think, that anyone who wants to request something, would at least put some effort in to write a decent request. This request lacks grammar and punctuation (although kudos for closing of with a period). Besides that, you give no reasons why you want to be assigned the Crat-role, other than: ''"I wanna again join the team amd and contribute to the wiki"''. As a former crat you know that you do not need to be a crat to contribute to the wiki. The role of the crat is not just to be able to action some decisive outcomes in conflicts, or to guard against vandalism. Most of that can be done already by the admins. The Crat/consul takes the final decision. It's a role of trust, and trust comes slowly, but is quickly lost.
I would suggest to start working on the wiki, and show your worth first.
I always wonder why people think "When I get that role, I will do...". It should be the other way around. A user should start working on a wiki, help out as much as possible, show that you are consistently available, make no arbitrary mistakes, and people will either nominate you, or when you then apply again, support the request.  Kind regards,   [[User:Rodejong|'''Rodejong''']]   [[User talk:Rodejong|💬 Talk]] [[:Special:Emailuser/Rodejong|✉️ Email]]  [[:Special:Contributions/Rodejong|📝 Edits]]  '''יהוה‎'''  [[File:Ponishare-verified.png|18px|link={{SERVER}}/wiki/mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong]][[mh:meta:Special:CentralAuth/Rodejong| Auth]]   11:15, 9 April 2025 (UTC) :{{oppose}} on several grounds. Firstly, the bar for bureaucrat has changed. It is a more clearly outlined position of responsibility and not just a hat after a very low margin, as it was previously. I would not recommend previous membership as an argument in favor unless proactive conduct can be used to support it. Secondly, I do not believe you have the track record of trustworthy conduct that the bureaucrat role wants from candidates. Off plaform is one thing but I am weary based on your record at Miraheze as well. A new account will only exacerbate this concern - to head off a repeat instance, you know what I'm talking about. Third, the request is poorly assembled, though I consider this the last priority. I recommend against attempts to acquire hats, and to instead improve your record both here and elsewhere instead. --'''[[User:Raidarr|raidarr]]''' '''('''[[User_talk:Raidarr|💬]]''')''' 14:40, 9 April 2025 (UTC) {{Discussion bottom}} == [[TestWiki:Request permissions]] be used only for sysop? == Hey folks! Should the [[TestWiki:Request permissions]] be updated to only include admin/sysop perms? Crat already requires a post here, we can ask for the same for IA as well (IA may not need inputs, and consuls can [not]grant at their own discretion). [[Template:Request instructions]] says that crat can be requested by just mentioning that in the template creation, but I think that's not the case anymore. If this passes, the userRights gadget and [[Template:RfP/preload]] can be updated to showcase only request for adminship. TLDR: Limit RfP to only sysop, maybe even move it to a different title, and require other groups IA and other groups to request by a post here (community portal). Open to any variations to the proposals [[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] ([[User talk:Bunnypranav|talk]]) 06:57, 12 April 2025 (UTC) :Yep, I agree that the template needs to be updated. [[User:Ternera|Ternera]] ([[User talk:Ternera|talk]]) 12:14, 12 April 2025 (UTC) ::@[[User:Ternera|Ternera]] What do you think about moving RfP to [[TestWiki:Request for adminship]] or a similar title? [[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] ([[User talk:Bunnypranav|talk]]) 12:29, 12 April 2025 (UTC) :::Supposedly confirmed user and autopatrolled rights can be requested at [[TestWiki:Request permissions]], so I don't know if that would be the best plan. I don't think I've ever seen anyone request those rights though since sysop is given out quite liberally. [[User:Ternera|Ternera]] ([[User talk:Ternera|talk]]) 12:33, 12 April 2025 (UTC) ::::I see. For now I have updated [[Template:RfP/preload]] to default to admin, and included a comment suggesting to change it if other groups are required. Same change has been done to [[Template:Request instructions]] [[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] ([[User talk:Bunnypranav|talk]]) 13:04, 12 April 2025 (UTC) :::::Excellent, thanks for your work! [[User:Ternera|Ternera]] ([[User talk:Ternera|talk]]) 13:07, 12 April 2025 (UTC) :I'm agree with Bunnypranav & Ternera. Confirmed user & autopatrolled rights can be requested at [[TestWiki:Request permissions]] while we can [[TestWiki:Request for adminship]] for admins request. Plus, we need to make some other options regarding other permissions. [[User:Sidrat al-Muntaha|Sidrat al-Muntaha]] ([[User talk:Sidrat al-Muntaha|talk]]) 18:15, 12 April 2025 (UTC) ::To keep it simple, I feel that it would be best to keep [[TestWiki:Request permissions]] as a catch all for all permission requests. The requester can always be advised to put the request for other options to a appropriate forum if available. That will keep us all in the loop with the changes. ::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 03:39, 24 April 2025 (UTC) == Proposal for Help:Abuse Filter to be converted into a non-test policy == I propose converting [[Help:Abuse Filter]] to [[TestWiki:Abuse filter]] and convert it into a non-test policy, and merge some of the other abuse filter-related pages into a single page: * [[TestWiki:Abuse filter operators]] * [[TestWiki:Abuse filter policy]] Similarly, I would also like to propose deleting [[Help:Abuse Filter rules]] given that we have [[:mw:Extension:AbuseFilter/Rules_format|a MediaWiki page for instructions on writing an abuse filter]]. [[User:Codename Noreste|'''''Codename Noreste''''']] ([[User talk:Codename Noreste|talk]]) 01:24, 15 April 2025 (UTC) :@[[User:Codename Noreste|Codename Noreste]] I have boldly redirected the help page to the mw: instruction page. Now we needn't delete it. ;) [[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] ([[User talk:Bunnypranav|talk]]) 08:42, 18 April 2025 (UTC) ::Until an editor comes along, I've added the related pages to [[Help:Abuse Filter#See also]] section. ::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 04:04, 24 April 2025 (UTC) == Interface and abuse filter operator changes == With the bureaucrat being a non testing permission, we should have a comment on the permissions between bureaucrat and consul. The interface admin can stay because you can test in your user space but the abuse filter operator should be between administrator and bureaucrat for testing the blocking feature on the abuse filter. ===Support=== {{Support}} my opinion [[User:GamerTester1080|GamerTester1080]] ([[User talk:GamerTester1080|talk]]) 09:15, 18 April 2025 (UTC) ===Neutral=== ===Oppose=== # {{Oppose}} Too complicated and unnecessary.
The more description that is provided to a label, the more likely it will be ignored or misunderstood.
Also, the policies have already been updated to reflect the change.
Also, the requesters will be made aware when they request permissions.
--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 04:16, 24 April 2025 (UTC) == Add extensions == Can I suggest these extension to be installed: [[MediaWikiWiki:Extension:AnonPrivacy]] for testing the extension with anonymous editing. [[MediaWikiWiki:Extension:DeletePagesForGood]] but only in category namespace. (The description of category namespace should be moved to category talk.) if a user moves to category namespace then deletes the page permanently, they can be banned through the move log. [[User:RandomNicknames|RandomNicknames]] ([[User talk:RandomNicknames|talk]]) 03:48, 19 April 2025 (UTC) :{{Not done}} To prevent abuse and to ensure adequate moderation capabilities neither extension will be enabled. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 04:18, 19 April 2025 (UTC) ::@[[User:Zppix|Zppix]] How does it prevent abuse. You can see the ip addresses in anonprivacy by using [[special:export]] and opening the xml file. For deletepagesforgood, you can create a namespace where you can’t move pages in and is used solely for deletion. [[User:RandomNicknames|RandomNicknames]] ([[User talk:RandomNicknames|talk]]) 06:25, 19 April 2025 (UTC) :::1) That is a huge barrier to preventing abuse from anon users. :::2) Deletepageforgood can easily be abused to mass delete pages with no way to restore. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 12:45, 19 April 2025 (UTC) ::::@[[User:Zppix|Zppix]] abuse to mass delete. You can create an isolated namespaces where you can’t move pages in used only for permanent deletion testing. [[User:RandomNicknames|RandomNicknames]] ([[User talk:RandomNicknames|talk]]) 19:54, 19 April 2025 (UTC) :::::Final answer is no. Zppix ([[:meta:User:Zppix|Meta]] | [[User talk:Zppix|talk to me]]) 22:28, 19 April 2025 (UTC) == Error in filter == I was trying to delete my userpage here to enable global user page, but the filter disallowed. Kindly assist, thank you. [[User:Jianhui67|Jianhui67]] ([[User talk:Jianhui67|talk]]) 06:52, 28 April 2025 (UTC) :Hey @[[User:Jianhui67|Jianhui67]], I have now deleted your user page. This seems to have been caused by a new edit filter for protection of user pages against vandalism (cc creator @[[User:Codename Noreste|Codename Noreste]]). [[User:Bunnypranav|Bunnypranav]] ([[User talk:Bunnypranav|talk]]) 07:51, 28 April 2025 (UTC) ::Ah, I see. Thanks for deleting! [[User:Jianhui67|Jianhui67]] ([[User talk:Jianhui67|talk]]) 09:02, 28 April 2025 (UTC) :::{{done|Disabled the filter accordingly}}. [[User:Codename Noreste|'''''Codename Noreste''''']] ([[User talk:Codename Noreste|talk]]) 16:07, 28 April 2025 (UTC) ::::... and fixed now. [[User:Codename Noreste|'''''Codename Noreste''''']] ([[User talk:Codename Noreste|talk]]) 16:19, 28 April 2025 (UTC) == Error in filter == What I was trying to do: I was trying to move my sandbox for test purpose) What message I received:This action has been automatically identified as harmful, and therefore disallowed. If you believe your action was constructive, please report this error at the community portal. A brief description of the abuse rule which your action matched is: User and user talk namespace disruption [[User:Vikram Singh344|Vikram Singh344]] ([[User talk:Vikram Singh344|talk]]) 08:37, 28 April 2025 (UTC) :{{done|Fixed so as to not affect your tests again}}. [[User:Codename Noreste|'''''Codename Noreste''''']] ([[User talk:Codename Noreste|talk]] · [[Special:Contributions/Codename Noreste|contribs]]) 06:08, 24 May 2025 (UTC) == Recent vandalism == There is a fair amount of vandalism from yesterday, that has yet to be undone, mostly because of the complex nature of trying to accurately unmerge page histories. Ultimately this is a Consul decision, but we could try and undo everything, which would be a lot of work, mostly from trying to figure out what goes where, or we could potentially restore from a database or XML backup, where we would inevitably lose some of the latest revisions. Again, this is up to consuls to decide, but we need to think about what would be more practical. [[User:MacFan4000|MacFan4000]] ([[User talk:MacFan4000|Talk]] [[Special:Contributions/MacFan4000|Contribs]]) 13:47, 28 April 2025 (UTC) :If the copy is merged, before any restoring from backup, perhaps review the contributions and identify all the users who contributed. :Then find the history of the contribution from the user's original and there should be a Diff. :Idk about what is practical but if you wish, I can take a look at the merged copy to see if there is a pattern. :--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 02:24, 29 April 2025 (UTC) ::From Revisions: ::[https://publictestwiki.com/wiki/User_talk:Void/mangled_page_history?diff=61326&oldid=61235 Reception123] ::[https://publictestwiki.com/wiki/User_talk:Void/mangled_page_history?diff=61524&oldid=61507 AlPaD] ::--- [[User:Imamy|Imamy]] ([[User talk:Imamy|talk]]) 02:54, 29 April 2025 (UTC) :::{{Ping|MacFan4000}} and {{Ping|Imamy}} Hello, I agree with restore the database and I understand that it's necessary [[User:AlPaD|AlPaD]] ([[User talk:AlPaD|talk]]) 17:07, 29 April 2025 (UTC) == Error in filter == I was trying to create a test page but filter disallowed me to page What message I received:This action has been automatically identified as harmful, and therefore disallowed.
